title: Design System: Orbit

ink.note: Three levels are used: ink for primary text and the primary button fill, ink-2 for body copy, ink-3 for labels and metadata. Dark-first: canonical is the value in the scheme the site presents by default, so it is the light ink. The full ramp is recorded here for tooling; only the three are used.

paper.note: Four surfaces: paper is the page, surface is a raised card, surface-2 a tinted block, sunken code. Dark-first, and canonical is the dark ground because that is the scheme the site presents by default. Warm off-black rather than #000: pure black is a value no display can render and it turns every step above it into a hole.

line.note: A divider that divides content. Exempt from the 3:1 boundary rule, which is why --line-2 exists.

line-2.note: 3.93:1 dark, 3.36:1 light on the page. The only value a control may be outlined with.

focus.note: The one hue in the system, because a ring the same colour as the text it surrounds is a ring nobody finds.

signal-bg.note: A state is a tint with dark text on it. The one-bit version painted state solid black, which made 'Prerelease' the loudest thing on the page.

shadow.note: Two levels, scheme-aware. Depth is a surface step first, a shadow second, and a border only when the element has no background of its own. The dark pair is black at a higher alpha rather than a lighter grey, because a shadow falls on the page outside the card and on a near-black ground the only way for one to register is to be darker than what it darkens. Declared as --elev-sm / --elev-md in each token block and mapped into Tailwind's --shadow-* namespace by @theme, since a same-named token in both places is settled by source order and the light scheme would silently take Tailwind's own default.

motion.note: One timing token and a stepped easing, because a one-bit machine's output did not tween. Anything that moves here is a discrete state change, and the only continuous motion on the site is the underline switching from dotted to solid, which is a decoration style change rather than an animation.

breakpoints.note: Two breakpoints, so the layout has three states rather than a continuous ramp. Continuity between them comes from the clamp() on the type scale, not from layout steps.

window.css: background-color: var(--surface); border-radius: var(--radius-lg); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm);
window.note: A raised block is a background step and a shadow, in that order. The two-value version drew a 1px full-contrast outline around six of these.

control-filled.html: Getting started
control-filled.css: background-color: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); height: 44px; border-radius: 0;
control-filled.note: The one legitimate inversion on the site. Hover is a 10% opacity step, not a colour, so it cannot fail contrast.

control-outlined.html: Read the docs
control-outlined.css: background-color: var(--paper); border: 1px solid var(--line); color: var(--ink); height: 44px; border-radius: 0;

chip.css: background-color: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); font-family: var(--font-mono); border-radius: 0;
chip.note: A tint, not an inversion. The one-bit version painted this solid black.

link.css: color: var(--ink); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-style: dotted; text-decoration-thickness: 2px; text-underline-offset: 0.2em;
link.note: The underline is the affordance. It goes solid on hover in 150ms, which is the only continuous motion in the system.

code-window.css: background-color: var(--code-bg); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 0;
code-window.note: The one place colour is allowed. Syntax colour is meaning rather than decoration, so the phosphor terminal keeps the measured palette from src/lib/code-theme.mjs.

card-inset.note: A tinted block with no border. Used for a platform row, a note, a callout.

narrative.northStar: Space and a background step separate things. A border is the last resort.
narrative.overview: A warm neutral system, dark-first: twelve measured values, four surfaces, three inks, two boundary weights, one focus hue, one state tint. The dark scheme is the ground the site is drawn on and the one it presents by default; light is the alternate, not the origin. Theme authority is ordered — a saved choice wins, then the system preference, and the site's own default sits underneath both as the answer for a browser that reports neither. Forcing dark ahead of the system would override an explicit preference and fails the test that asserts the page honours one. This replaced a two-value one-bit palette with a 2px stipple standing in for every tone, and the replacement is not a regression but the difference between a constraint and a design. The two-value version turned its own rule into the answer: seven full-contrast borders and six outlined surfaces so nothing was distinguished, twenty-one uses of a stipple that read as noise, square corners everywhere so shape carried nothing, solid black rectangles to say 'Prerelease', and rules touching the text they divided.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, not cold, and dark by default: the page is #0a0a0b rather than black or the usual #121212 slate, so a raised card reads as a card and not as a hole.
Two boundary weights and only two: a hairline that divides content, and one that clears 3:1 for a control. Nothing at full contrast.
Three inks for three real levels of information, not three decorative shades.
One focus hue, because a ring the same colour as the text it surrounds is a ring nobody finds.
A state is a tint with dark text on it, never a solid fill.
The code window is the one place colour is allowed, because syntax colour is meaning rather than decoration.
do: Separate with space or a surface step first; reach for a border last.
Give every rule air on both sides, written as a pair with the previous section's bottom.
Repoint a third-party colour at one of the twelve tokens the moment it appears.
Mark a state with a label as well as a tint.
Keep the code window's syntax palette measured rather than chosen by eye.
dont: Draw anything at full contrast. A 100% black or white border is a bug.
Use a solid fill for small information; the primary button is the only inversion.
Bring back the stipple, the dither, or a square corner.
Set a typeface at a size it cannot carry. No automated check can catch this: three pixel metrics were measured against four faces and the failing face scored higher on all three.

Remap --sl-color-white to a surface; Starlight sets every heading's colour from it, and pointing it at the ground made all eleven documentation titles invisible. That passed both the palette check and axe.
Trust that a palette implies legible text.

display.replaced: Workbench, a bitmap face drawn for 8-12px and illegible at the 64px display size

typography.automatedLegibilityCheck: None, deliberately. Three pixel metrics were written and measured against four faces at 64px; the bitmap face scored higher on all three, because its blocks touch and its band is taller and denser than a real face's. A statistic cannot tell a reader that a word does not spell anything. tests/typography.spec.ts keeps the two checks that are true: the declared face is the loaded face, and no line has its ink cut by its own line box.

description: A warm neutral system, dark-first, where space and a background step separate things, and a border is the last resort.
